title: Senior Infrastructure Engineer
description_html:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.



We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.



We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.



If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.



About This Role:

We are seeking a Software Engineer to join Crusoe’s Hardware Systems Engineering team and build the tools, automation, and data platforms that let our hardware engineers debug, validate, and support high-performance compute systems at scale. In this role, you will own the software that supports the full hardware lifecycle, from prototype bring-up through large-scale production, accelerating issue resolution and improving reliability across Crusoe Cloud’s GPU- and CPU-based infrastructure.

You will work closely with hardware engineers to understand their debugging and validation workflows, then turn them into automatable workflows. You will also work with cross-functional teams to integrate tools with the production environment. A particular focus will be provisioning, hardware health monitoring, test framework, and data collection. Your work will directly improve Crusoe’s ability to deploy and operate sustainable, AI-first compute systems with world-class performance and reliability.



What You’ll Be Working On:

 - Design, build, and maintain software tools and frameworks that support the hardware development and sustaining lifecycle, including bring-up, validation, deployment, and ongoing production support.

 - Develop automated test, diagnostics, and health-monitoring frameworks that run across fleets of servers, enabling continuous reliability improvements.

 - Build tooling, monitoring and logging systems that help hardware engineers triage and root-cause issues across different hardware platforms.

 - Create automated validation and characterization workflows for GPU, CPU, and high-performance compute platforms, including result collection, analysis, and reporting.

 - Build and operate data pipelines, dashboards, and analytics that surface hardware failure trends, performance regressions, and reliability metrics.

 - Support E2E integration and solution testing by developing test harnesses and CI/CD workflows that ensure Crusoe Cloud products meet performance, reliability, and scalability expectations.

 - Evaluate and introduce new tools, testing methods, and automation approaches that improve engineering efficiency and support Crusoe’s sustainability goals.

 - Provide data-driven insights from tooling and telemetry to influence Crusoe’s hardware roadmap and reliability strategy.



What You’ll Bring to the Team:

 - 5+ years of professional software engineering experience, ideally building internal tools, infrastructure software, provisioning, test automation, or systems software.

 - Strong proficiency in Python and at least one systems language (Go, C/C++, or Rust), plus Shell scripting.

 - Experience designing and implementing automation and test frameworks, including workflow engines, for hardware or large-scale infrastructure.

 - Experience with BMC/Redfish/IPMI, firmware update automation, or out-of-band management.

 - Experience with fleet management, provisioning, or large-scale automation tools (Kubernetes, Ansible, Terraform, etc.).

 - Experience building data pipelines, logging, telemetry, or observability tooling to analyze system behavior at scale.

 - Experience working across hardware, firmware, and software teams in multidisciplinary environments.

 - Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with a data-driven approach.

 - Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to gather requirements from engineers and external partners and translate them into usable tools.

 - Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or equivalent experience.



Bonus Points:

 - Experience building tooling for GPU clusters, including GPU-to-GPU communication diagnostics (NCCL tests, NVLink monitoring, etc.).

 - Familiarity with PCIe, InfiniBand, and NVMe/storage concepts and tooling (e.g., lspci, ibstat, nvme-cli, perftest, fio), with the curiosity to go deeper.

 - Working knowledge of Linux systems, including kernel interfaces, drivers, device tooling, and low-level system diagnostics.

 - Familiarity with NVIDIA tooling such as DCGM, NVML, and fabric management software.

 - Experience supporting both ARM and x86 server architectures.

 - Background in factory test, manufacturing test software, or hardware qualification workflows.




COMPENSATION RANGE:

Compensation will be paid in the range of $170,000 - $205,000. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicants knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

title: Principal Platform Engineer – Kubernetes Reliability and Distributed Systems
description_html: Principal Platform Engineer – Kubernetes Reliability and Distributed Systems          This role has been designed as 'Hybrid' with a requirement that you will work on average 2 days per week from an HPE office.                    Who We Are:                               Hewlett Packard Enterprise is the global edge-to-cloud company advancing the way people live and work. We help companies connect, protect, analyze, and act on their data and applications wherever they live, from edge to cloud, so they can turn insights into outcomes at the speed required to thrive in today’s complex world. Our culture thrives on finding new and better ways to accelerate what’s next. We know varied backgrounds are valued and succeed here. We have the flexibility to manage our work and personal needs. We make bold moves, together, and are a force for good. If you are looking to stretch and grow your career our culture will embrace you. Open up opportunities with HPE.                     Job Description:         Role overview   We are seeking a Principal Platform Engineer with deep expertise in Kubernetes, distributed systems, and highly available infrastructure to help evolve and operate the Object Storage platform.  This role will own the most complex platform-level technical challenges, including Kubernetes scheduling and resource management, pod failover, service discovery and load balancing, control-plane availability, node failure recovery, timeout behavior, and system resilience during degraded operating conditions.  The successful candidate will work across engineering teams to establish clear ownership, diagnose complex production issues, guide architectural decisions, and build scalable, reliable platform capabilities. This is a hands-on technical leadership role that requires both deep implementation experience and the ability to influence engineering practices across the organization.    Key responsibilities    Serve as the senior technical authority for Kubernetes platform architecture, reliability, and operational behavior.  Own the investigation and resolution of complex issues involving:  Pod failover and rescheduling  Service availability and load balancing  Control Plane operation as well as Node failover  Network, API, and service timeouts  Resource requests, limits, quotas, scheduling, affinity, taints, tolerations, and workload pinning  Cluster capacity, performance, and scaling  Distributed-system failure modes and recovery behavior    Define and drive improvements to Kubernetes high availability, fault tolerance, and disaster-recovery strategies.  Establish clear technical ownership and operating models for platform capabilities.  Lead architecture, design, and implementation of platform improvements across multiple engineering teams.  Develop repeatable approaches for diagnosing failures across application, Kubernetes, networking, storage, and infrastructure layers.  Improve observability, including metrics, logs, traces, alerts, dashboards, and health indicators for platform services.  Define and monitor service-level objectives and reliability measures for platform components.  Lead or support major incident response, root-cause analysis, and corrective-action programs.  Identify systemic issues rather than treating incidents as isolated events.  Create technical standards, reference architectures, runbooks, and operational best practices.  Mentor senior engineers and raise the organization’s expertise in Kubernetes and distributed systems.  Partner with application, infrastructure, networking, security, and operations teams to resolve cross-functional issues.  Evaluate new Kubernetes capabilities and platform technologies and determine where they provide meaningful value.  Balance short-term incident resolution with long-term architectural improvements.     Required qualifications    Significant experience designing, building, and operating production Kubernetes platforms.  Deep understanding of Kubernetes architecture and core components, including:  API server and control-plane services  Scheduler and controller manager  Nodes, kubelet, and container runtimes  Services, endpoints, ingress, and load balancing  Resource requests and limits  Quality of Service classes  Affinity, anti-affinity, taints, tolerations, and topology constraints  Pod disruption budgets and workload availability  Kubelet and CRI (containerd)    Strong knowledge of high-availability and failure-recovery patterns for distributed systems.  Demonstrated experience troubleshooting complex production failures involving Kubernetes, networking, infrastructure, and application services.  Experience diagnosing Kubernetes failover behavior, service timeouts, partial failures, network partitions, and degraded cluster states.  Experience with Kubernetes cluster upgrade process.  Strong understanding of Linux systems, networking, DNS, TCP/IP, containers, and storage fundamentals.  Experience with cloud or on-premises infrastructure and infrastructure-as-code practices.  Proficiency in Go, Python, and Bash programming or scripting language.  Experience developing automation, platform tooling, or operational frameworks.  Strong observability and reliability engineering experience using metrics, logs, traces, alerting, and performance analysis.  Demonstrated ability to lead complex technical initiatives across organizational boundaries.  Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex technical issues to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.  Ability to operate effectively during high-severity incidents and drive issues through root cause and permanent resolution.     Preferred qualifications    Experience contributing to or extending Kubernetes, container-runtime, networking, or infrastructure projects.  Experience with Kubernetes distributions such as EKS, AKS, GKE, OpenShift, or upstream Kubernetes.  Experience with service meshes, ingress controllers, CNI plugins, CSI storage systems, or cluster-autoscaling technologies.  Experience with distributed databases, consensus systems, or control-plane technologies such as etcd.  Experience designing multi-cluster, multi-region, or edge-oriented Kubernetes environments.  Knowledge of Linux performance analysis, kernel behavior, and container isolation.  Experience with chaos engineering, failure injection, load testing, and resilience testing.  Experience establishing SLOs, error budgets, production-readiness reviews, and reliability governance.  Experience working in an environment with embedded, edge, fleet, or geographically distributed systems.  Familiarity with GitOps and deployment technologies such as Argo CD, Flux, Helm, or similar tools.  Relevant Kubernetes or cloud certifications, such as CKA, CKAD, or equivalent practical experience.     Principal-level expectations   The person hired into this role should be expected to:   Own problems that cross team and technology boundaries.  Make architecture decisions that affect the broader platform and product roadmap.  Establish technical direction rather than only implement assigned designs.  Drive ambiguous, high-impact issues from symptoms through root cause and permanent resolution.  Create reusable platform capabilities and engineering standards.  Influence without relying on direct authority.  Mentor other senior engineers and improve the organization’s technical maturity.  Remain hands-on enough to debug systems, prototype solutions, review code, and validate designs.           Accessibility    HPE is committed to creating an inclusive and accessible workplace and encourages applications from all qualified individuals, including those with disabilities.
